draws_source.object: theta: 20000 x 774 matrix of per-LGA prevalence draws, joint across areas
draws_source.note: joint draws, so the spatial dependence between areas is preserved; no independence approximation was needed

estimand_a_count_of_lgas.construction: identified set [C_O, C_O + 120] given one realisation of the 654 observed-LGA statuses, C_O = #{s in O : theta_s > 0.50}

estimand_b_population_share.estimand: population share living in an LGA with theta > 0.50
estimand_b_population_share.construction: Manski bounds [p*pi_O, p*pi_O + (1-p)] at each draw, p the population share held by observed LGAs, pi_O the observed-population weighted share above the line; no assumption on unobserved LGAs

monotonicity_variant.assumption: unclustered LGAs are assumed no better than observed ones, pi_U >= pi_O; this is an assumption about Nigeria that these data cannot test

interval_interpretation.object: a 95% posterior interval for the sample-analogue identified set
interval_interpretation.note: This is NOT an Imbens-Manski (2004) confidence set. That object controls frequentist coverage of the identified set under moment inequalities for a consistent set estimator. What is computed here is the 2.5th percentile of the lower bound and the 97.5th percentile of the upper bound across 20,000 posterior draws. In all three cases reported, both bounds are non-decreasing functions of one draw-level quantity (C_O, or pi_O), so the identified set lies inside the reported interval exactly when that quantity lies in its own central 95% interval: the containment statement carries 95% posterior mass. It carries no frequentist coverage guarantee, and it conditions on the model for theta in the observed LGAs being right, which is what the paper is arguing about; it also treats p as known and the observed/unobserved split as exact, so cluster-to-LGA assignment error is not in these bounds.
